notes: CRITICAL SPECIES CAVEAT: the only numeric half-lives in this paper (0.4249 h for 64Cu-DOTA-F56 and 6.967 h for 64Cu-DOTA-F56-CM) were measured in female Sprague-Dawley RATS, not in mice. The body explicitly explains the choice: 'Because albumin has a half-life of 1.9 days in rats and 1.0 day in mice, we selected old female Sprague-Dawley rats... for the single-dose pharmacokinetic study.' The mouse experiment in the PK section was a qualitative Western blot of albumin conjugation, with no PK parameters. There is a dose discrepancy for F56-CM in mice: Methods give '5 mg/mL in PBS, injection volume, 10 mL/kg' while the Fig. 4A caption gives '5 mg/kg'; both are recorded verbatim and no arithmetic conversion was performed. A further internal inconsistency: Methods state the blood PK parameters 'were analyzed using a two-compartmental model' whereas Results attribute them to 'statistical moments analysis'; no phase label is attached to either half-life, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' for both radiolabelled agents. Biodistribution %IA/g values at 4 h and 8 h in tumour-bearing nude mice are reported (Fig. 4E-F) but are not Cmax/AUC parameters and are not entered in the PK fields. Statements about albumin half-lives in mice, rats, rabbits and humans (1, 1.9, 5.55, 19 days) are cited background, not measurements from this study.
